summary.intent: Evaluate which plugin agents should move to Fable 5.1, find why the pipeline misses architectural issues, and fix it. Then review Codex's new marketplace infrastructure and get both pieces of work into PRs.
summary.outcome: Added a Fable-tier scribe/audit-architecture stage with arch-model@1 and arch-audit@1 schemas. Moved persisted artifacts from .claude/ to docs/ and persisted plan@1. PR #3 merged. Reviewed Codex work, added a mason bump and changelog, opened PR #5, and resolved its rebase conflicts with CI passing.

repo: Version bumps must agree across plugin.json, README **Version:** line, top CHANGELOG ## [x.y.z] entry and marketplace.json, enforced by scripts/check-versions.sh. Codex-native manifests under harnesses/codex/ must also match, or the integrity check fails.
Every **BREAKING** changelog label in this repo pairs with a major bump, so a minor bump must not use it.
THE SYSTEM SHALL is the ecosystem-wide EARS phrasing in agent <output> sections; mason/scaffolder.md is the lone outlier. Agents' <constitution> blocks must be byte-identical.
mason/README.md's Conformance Checks table is the source of truth for mason:auditor, so new model tiers like claude-fable-5-1 must be added there.

shared/agent-best-practices.md claimed a terminal architectural exit gate that never existed. Pipeline checks were all spec-vs-spec or narrow code slices, so nothing checked a spec against the whole system.
scribe/architect is reactive: it fires only after ranger confirms a finding. It produces spec@1, so arch-spec@1 is effectively orphaned.
dist/codex is generated by tools/build-codex-marketplace.py and verified with --check, which is also a CI gate. Never hand-edit it, and watch for stray dist/.codex.build-* temp dirs getting staged.
Doc-only README changes need no version bump, but changes to mason's own skill logic do.
Many plugin files referenced .claude/specs; the rename also touched constitution.md, workspace-conventions.md, gate-spec, and three schemas.

code.finding: Stated a model-homogeneous-lanes philosophy with Opus only at a terminal architectural exit gate that did not exist; rewritten to name Sonnet/Opus/Fable lanes.
Carries a spec_file_path field that needed the new docs/ path convention.
Holds the canonical persistence rules for spec paths that were updated from .claude/specs to docs/specs.

workflow: Re-verifying against repo precedent (changelog BREAKING convention, EARS phrasing across 38+ agents) caught drift that the first self-review missed.
Checking merge-base and ancestor relationships showed an earlier claim about unpushed commits was wrong, and no rebase was needed. Verify git state before reporting it.
Staging with git add -A swept in scratch build output; review the staged list before committing.
GitHub mergeable/mergeStateStatus is computed asynchronously and shows UNKNOWN or UNSTABLE briefly, so poll it rather than treating it as a conflict.
When two independently authored copies of a file conflict, treat the one from the dedicated reviewed PR as canonical and additively keep any non-contradictory content from the other.

friction: Volume-vs-difficulty reasoning for Fable assignment shifted across several turns before landing on a missing pipeline stage rather than a model swap.
Subagent report claimed a duplicate </output> tag in architect.md that did not exist.
Mis-stated that local main was 6 commits ahead and blocking, then had to correct it after checking ancestry.
A stray dist/.codex.build-* temp dir was staged and had to be removed.
PR #5 hit conflicts because PR #4 (a separate Wisp Plugins rebrand) merged first. The ADR-010 add/add conflict needed manual merging.
The `find dist` output appeared empty because of the shell wrapper, which caused a brief false alarm.
A weaker earlier check ran only 'search for @ usage' in Codex docs and briefly produced conflicting evidence about plugin@marketplace syntax.
open_items: Decide whether the Codex-native audit-architecture skill should keep requiring explicit user authorization before persisting arch-model, or whether the Claude version should match. Neither side has recorded it as an intentional divergence.
Revisit bumping navigator/planner to opus/xhigh if plan quality stays weak now that audit-architecture exists. It was shelved for now.
Possibly raise navigator/challenger effort if it misses issues; it was left at sonnet.
Merge PR #5 once GitHub mergeability settles from UNKNOWN back to MERGEABLE; CI passed.
Local main carries an unrelated unpushed commit (3f6024a, v3.5.3 full-repo sweep) that was left untouched.
An independent review (/code-review or mason:auditor) of the changed files was suggested, because not every constitution rule was checked line by line against every touched file.
